lines.trans: Hello! I'm not a journalist. I'm the head of Ivan Samsonov's campaign.
I've come to bring you our deepest apologies.
Now that is nerve! You are not blind, after all.
Do you see what he did here? He will lose the election now!
No, our candidate is very ashamed of this.
Why are we even listening? That bribe-taker Anikeev is with them!
Arkady Borisovich is a very experienced politician. And he didn't take bribes.
He always supported disabled people!
For fifteen years we've been asking for a new building! Anikeev came here in person, and what?

examples.text: Я пришла принести вам наши самые глубокие извинения.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('experienced').

examples.text: Слушай, Самсон, я тут подумал. Твой начальник — такой опытный специалист.

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'держивать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to support', paired with 'поддержать'.

examples.trans: And does the governor support you?

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'писывать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to sign', paired with 'подписать'.

examples.trans: The director is signing the documents.

examples.text: Я их ещё два года назад им выделил! Я сам приказ подписывал!
examples.trans: I allocated it to them two years ago! I signed the order myself!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'литик'). Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'politician' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich is a very experienced politician.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович — очень опытный политик. И он взяток не брал.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'обещать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to promise', paired with 'обещать'.

examples.text: Он сегодня пообещал построить нам новое здание.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'нести'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to bring (carrying)', paired with 'приносить'.

meanings.note: Agent/instrument noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-тель' ('-er'). Common masculine noun meaning 'head, leader, manager' in everyday Russian.

meanings.note: once; что скажешь? = what do you say?

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'красть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to steal', paired with 'красть'.

points at something: это моё = that's mine
